headline: OpenAI has raised the default context size of its GPT-6.1 Sol model in Codex and ChatGPT Work from 272,000 to 500,000 tokens and dropped long-context surcharges for subscribers.
score_reason: Kept at 6: new on 11 Oct 2026, article read in full; it is a settings change reported by one outlet.
importance_line: Paying ChatGPT and Codex users who give Sol long coding or research jobs get more working room by default and no extra charge for long inputs, but the article names no OpenAI document for the change and offers no evidence yet on how well the model uses the extra room.
summary: Crypto Briefing reports that from 11 Oct 2026 OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol, launched on 29 Sep 2026, starts with a 500,000-token context length, the amount of text it can keep in view at once, in Codex (OpenAI's coding tool) and ChatGPT Work, up from 272,000, and that long-context surcharges were dropped for subscription users. The model's maximum stays at 1,050,000 tokens, and the API rates Crypto Briefing lists are $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens.
notes: Read Crypto Briefing in full. No OpenAI primary source seen; an aggregator headline says the Codex head announced it.
